title: Disposition reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts under the new permanent-evidence policy
description:
Applies AGENTS.md "Permanent Test Evidence" and docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md
"From observation to finding" (both landed in PR #553, merge commit 3f5693a0) to one
piece of existing proof machinery: packages/core/test/reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts.

CENTRAL QUESTION: which responsibilities in that file justify permanent executable
evidence, and which assertions merely turn editable policy prose into executable
snapshots of itself?

PROBLEM. The file is 318 lines, 17 tests, ~60 assertions. Most have the shape
  policy prose -> regex asserting the policy still contains equivalent prose
which is recursive proof machinery: an authorized bad policy edit simply updates
both the document and the regex, while a legitimate equivalent rewording breaks the
regex. That is a false-failure generator, not evidence.

ORIGINAL AUTHORITY, checked: eshyra-w65u acceptance criteria authorized "a lightweight
policy test pins the essential distinctions" around the abandoned eshyra-review-v2
machinery; eshyra-o9bd.19.1.18 authorized a "lightweight extension" when the canonical
policy document was introduced. Neither authorized executable semantic ownership of
the review policy, and neither makes every later assertion permanent.

SCOPE: this file only. beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts has the same defect class and is
explicitly OUT of scope here; file it separately if the analysis holds.

EXCLUSIONS. No replacement policy schema, snapshot, policy hash, manifest, generated
baseline, approval marker, certification file, or new checker. Do not move the same
semantic mirrors into another test file. Do not create a registry of required policy
sentences. Do not replace ten regexes with one giant regex. No new proof machinery to
prove the old proof machinery was safely removed.

Effective review profile: semantic-system. This changes durable proof responsibilities
around repository review authority.

Also in scope: disposition the AGENTS.md sentence "Proof machinery ... is implementation
and needs its own tests, but it does not inherit the proof burden of the product."
Determine whether "needs its own tests" materially creates an unintended universal
test obligation that recurses one level outward. Narrow it only if it does.
notes:
DISPOSITION LEDGER (2026-09-22), format: existing evidence -> claimed invariant -> authority -> actual boundary -> disposition -> replacement.
Blanket replacement responsibility for every RETIRED prose assertion: semantic correctness of repository review policy is owned by the authority hierarchy (AGENTS.md + docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md), the owning Bead or accepted design, and semantic-system review of any change to that authority. A regex copy of editable authority cannot establish that a FUTURE version of that authority is valid: an authorized bad edit updates document and regex together, while a legitimate rewording breaks the regex. Demonstrated empirically - see ADVERSARIAL EVIDENCE below.

RETAINED / CONSOLIDATED (4 tests, 8 assertions):
1. 'points common authority at a review policy document that exists' <- old test 1. Invariant: AGENTS.md's pointer to the canonical policy resolves to a real file. Authority: AGENTS.md 'PR Review Authority and Lifecycle' makes the linked document mandatory; a dangling pointer makes the obligation unfollowable. Boundary: two independently editable artifacts plus the link between them. STRENGTHENED: the path is now parsed FROM the AGENTS.md link instead of hardcoded, so renaming the document with its pointer updated passes (the old file FAILED that good edit) and renaming it with the pointer left dangling fails (the old file could not detect it). The prose mirror of 'Anyone authorizing a design...' is retired.
2. 'keeps CLAUDE.md loading AGENTS.md instead of owning policy itself' <- old test 16. Invariant: CLAUDE.md still carries the @AGENTS.md import. Authority: CLAUDE.md is the Claude Code entry point and AGENTS.md is the single source. Boundary: an executable import mechanism, not prose. Consequence of loss: sessions stop loading repository authority entirely, whatever either document says.
3. 'does not revive the abandoned PR #481 review machinery' <- consolidates old tests 3, 6, 16-negatives and 17. Invariant: eshyra-review-v2 / REVIEW CONTRACT / contract hash absent from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; no review:* script in ANY workspace manifest; no docs/review/ protocol directory. Authority: eshyra-w65u acceptance criteria, which this file was created to serve; bd memory pr481-review-contract-framework-superseded. Boundary: executable command surface, repository tree shape, and common-authority text. STRENGTHENED two ways: script scan now covers packages/core and packages/cli manifests (the old test saw only root), and docs/review/ is now checked at all. Note the canonical policy document is deliberately NOT scanned - it legitimately names eshyra-review-v2 to record it as superseded. Concrete harm this prevents recurring: PR #504 was rejected solely for lacking these absent artifacts.
4. 'keeps the disposition gate ahead of findings discipline' <- old test 11 (ordering assertion only). Invariant: '## From observation to finding' precedes '## Findings discipline'. Authority: the policy section's own text states it runs before findings discipline and the gate only functions upstream of what it gates. Boundary: actual document topology, checked against the claim - not a copy of the claim. Retained because a gate placed after the stage it gates is not a gate, and no other mechanism encodes that relation structurally. Both headings are now existence-checked so a deleted section fails rather than silently passing on indexOf -1.

RETIRED (13 tests, 57 assertions), all semantic mirrors of editable authority:
old 2 (AGENTS.md section order between Git & PR Workflow and Beads Issue Tracker) - no authority requires that placement; it was an eshyra-w65u DELIVERY criterion, not a durable invariant; reordering AGENTS.md sections is a harmless editorial change.
old 4 (owning bead implies no formatted contract), old 5 (profiles select depth), old 6-prose (PR #481 not active authority), old 7 (authority precedence both sides, incl. the historical 'ChatGPT Project' negative), old 8 (process-transition exception), old 9 (exact-head and bounded-vs-full rereview), old 10 (findings discipline), old 11-prose (disposition gate clauses), old 12 (search undiminished), old 13 (permanent-evidence clauses in AGENTS.md), old 14 (DESIGN_INVALIDATED lifecycle), old 15 (PR handoff prose + a DRY negative already owned by beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts).
old 3-partial: 'single owner', not-DESIGN_INVALIDATED and the profile-string negative retired as DRY prose mirrors; the abandoned-machinery negatives survive in retained test 3.

NOT USED as justification anywhere: 'this assertion once caught a bad edit.' Old test 9's two-cycle assertion did catch a real edit during PR #553, and three of old test 13's assertions were written by me one day earlier. Neither fact makes them appropriate PERMANENT evidence, which is exactly the distinction AGENTS.md 'Permanent Test Evidence' draws.

ADVERSARIAL EVIDENCE (empirical, both directions):
BAD states that FAIL: policy doc renamed with the AGENTS.md link left dangling; CLAUDE.md loses @AGENTS.md; AGENTS.md reintroduces a REVIEW CONTRACT / contract hash; a review:contract script added to packages/core/package.json (old test could not see this); docs/review/ recreated; the disposition gate relocated after findings discipline.
GOOD states that PASS: policy document renamed WITH its pointer updated (old file failed this); and four clauses the old file pinned reworded equivalently - 'Approval binds to an exact head SHA', 'If a defect is worth fixing ever...', 'Profiles select review depth', 'A process transition may omit the process it replaces'. Under that identical harmless rewording the OLD file reported 4 failed / 13 passed and the NEW file 4 passed. That is the false-failure generator this task removed.

AGENTS.md WORDING CHANGE, dispositioned before editing: 'Proof machinery ... is implementation and needs its own tests, but it does not inherit the proof burden of the product.' MATERIAL, so narrowed. 'needs its own tests' is unconditional and recurses - the tests are themselves proof machinery, so they would need their own tests (measureRun.test.ts is already a live instance of proof machinery for proof machinery). It also contradicted the same section's proportionality clause, the immediately following 'Test it in proportion to the decisions it gates', and this very change, which removes proof machinery WITHOUT adding tests to prove the removal safe. Replaced with: machinery is implementation and does not inherit the product's proof burden; give it evidence proportionate to the decisions it gates; that is often a test but not automatically one. NO new assertion was added for this wording change - under the disposition above, prose assertions over AGENTS.md are precisely what is being retired, and adding one would reinstate the recursion.

OUT OF SCOPE, filed separately: packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts carries the same defect class.

MEASUREMENTS: file 318 -> 121 lines, 17 -> 4 tests, 65 -> 8 expect() calls. Wall clock 102/105/97ms -> 87/86/88ms (3 runs each); runtime was never the problem and is not the justification. Suite 5,604 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed, 13 fewer tests than main. verify:worktree clean.
Sibling filed: eshyra-5wbx for beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts (same defect class, deliberately out of scope here).
PR #558 opened (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/558), head a200b757, branch eshyra-4tgd. Stays in_progress until that PR merges, per AGENTS.md Session Completion.
RETIRED bd memory pr481-review-contract-framework-superseded (2026-09-22). It was the largest hot-path carrier of the abandoned design: bd prime injects it into EVERY agent session, and it taught the full PR #481 vocabulary and architecture - protocol name, hashed REVIEW CONTRACT bead sections, contract hashes, authorization checkpoints, mirrored GitHub contract comments, docs/review/eshyra-development-and-review-protocol.md, review:classify/preflight/handoff/checkpoint/invalidate, and .github/workflows/review-governance.yml. Its second half restated the current lifecycle, which AGENTS.md and docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md now own in full.
REPLACEMENT RESPONSIBILITY: never-adopted proposals create no current obligations; current review requirements are determined by current accepted repository authority. The specific protection it carried - that no review contract/hash/checkpoint/certification artifact may be demanded - survives POSITIVELY in the policy intro, which now reads that such an artifact 'is required only where current accepted authority explicitly requires it for the work at hand', plus the existing 'the absence of an unrequired artifact is never grounds to reject a PR' under Authority and required context. That is what actually prevented PR #504's false rejection; the vocabulary lesson was not.
PROVENANCE PRESERVED, not rewritten: closed PR #481, bead eshyra-o9bd.19.1.17, bead eshyra-w65u, this bead, and Dolt/Git history. No tombstone memory, registry, or appendix was created to replace it.
REPAIR OF PR #558 HEAD a200b757 (2026-09-22). Review conclusion adopted: do not improve the permanent model of PR #481 - remove that model from current operational authority and proof machinery. A never-adopted proposal needs no permanent exception saying it is not authority.

REPLACEMENT RESPONSIBILITY for every retired PR #481 guard: never-adopted proposals create no current obligations. Current review requirements are determined by current accepted repository authority. Historical Git/PR/Bead records preserve provenance when investigation is needed. The absence of PR #481 machinery is NOT a permanent contract and is not described as one anywhere.

1. RETIRED the anti-authority guard 'does not revive the abandoned PR #481 review machinery' in full, with its ABANDONED_MACHINERY and WORKSPACE_MANIFESTS constants and every comment teaching the suite about eshyra-review-v2, REVIEW CONTRACT, contract hashes, review:*, or docs/review/. No replacement blacklist, broader file list, renamed detector, registry, hash, manifest, or permission test. The generic review:* and docs/review/ namespaces are no longer reserved: future review tooling is judged against the accepted authority existing when it is proposed, and resemblance to PR #481 is not itself a defect.

2. CURRENT AUTHORITY, docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md intro, only occurrence in the hot path. REMOVED 'The eshyra-review-v2 machinery proposed on PR #481 closed unmerged and is not repository authority' and the negative enumeration that taught its vocabulary. RETAINED as positive rule: 'A review contract, hash, authorization comment, checkpoint, certification, mirrored comment, command, or other review artifact is required only where current accepted authority explicitly requires it for the work at hand. Only current accepted authority creates requirements; a proposal that was never adopted creates none.' Same operative semantics, no historical dependency. AGENTS.md needed no change - it carried zero references, verified. Retained WITHOUT change because they are positive and carry no #481 identity: profiles 'do not create a contract, hash, checkpoint, or authorization artifact' (Review profiles); 'It needs no specially formatted review contract ... and the absence of an unrequired artifact is never grounds to reject a PR' (Authority and required context); 'These are review duties, not new checkpoint artifacts' (Findings discipline).

3. HISTORY PRESERVED, nothing rewritten: closed PR #481, beads eshyra-o9bd.19.1.17 and eshyra-w65u, audit and history documents, Git/Dolt history all still record what happened. No tombstone memory, registry, or appendix created.

4. POINTER GUARD REPAIRED. The a200b757 version parsed the path out of the human-readable link LABEL, so changing display text failed while the target stayed valid, and pointing that label at any existing file passed. Replaced with a label-free structural assertion: every repo-relative Markdown link in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md resolves. External URLs and bare fragments are excluded. No schema, hash or manifest was invented; the identity used is the link target itself, which is already machine-checkable.

5. REMAINING GUARDS RE-EVALUATED. RETAINED 'keeps CLAUDE.md loading AGENTS.md': invariant is the @AGENTS.md import; authority is CLAUDE.md as the Claude Code entry point with AGENTS.md as single source; boundary is an executable import mechanism, not a sentence; bad state is silent and severe (sessions stop loading authority at all); executable evidence adds real independent value because a reviewer can miss the deletion. RETAINED the link-resolution guard on the same grounds: a dangling authority pointer is silent, easy to miss in a diff, and makes an obligation unfollowable.
RETIRED 'keeps the disposition gate ahead of findings discipline'. Applying the six-point test honestly: it identifies both sections by heading TEXT, so renaming either heading - a harmless editorial edit - fails it. That makes it a sibling of the very defect class this repair closes: permanent proof machinery encoding a textual proxy rather than an independently meaningful invariant. Its bad state is a single-document section move, fully visible in the diff, so executable evidence adds nothing independent of semantic-system review of that document. Replacement responsibility: the policy document's internal consistency is owned by semantic-system review of changes to it. I flagged this guard at PR #558 handoff as my most challengeable retention; the sharpened standard resolves it.

SIBLING SEARCH within the file and the authority touched here: the heading-text proxy above was the only remaining instance of the class. The surviving two assertions use no document text as identity.

AGENTS.md proof-machinery narrowing from a200b757 RETAINED unchanged; no executable assertion pins it, and none was added.

MEASUREMENTS. Guard file across this repair: 121 -> 77 lines, 4 -> 2 tests, 8 -> 2 expect(). Across the whole bead: 318 -> 77 lines, 17 -> 2 tests, 65 -> 2 expect(). Suite 5,602 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed, 15 fewer than main.

ADVERSARIAL. Bad states that FAIL: CLAUDE.md stops loading common authority; the canonical policy renamed with its pointer left stale; an ADR link rots (sibling of the same class, now covered). Good states that PASS: link display text changed with the target intact - the a200b757 guard reported 2 failed on exactly this, the new one passes; policy document renamed WITH its pointer updated. No test was added demonstrating that review:* or docs/review/ names are permitted; the blacklist was removed, not inverted.

MATERIALITY: bounded repair. Current review semantics are unchanged - every rule the removed sentences carried survives positively. No fresh full semantic-system review is required on that ground.
FAIL-OPEN DEFECT found by bounded re-review of the repaired mechanism at 552c0d36, before merge; fixed at bc277005.
repositoryLinkTargets read only INLINE Markdown links. Reference-style links ([label][ref] plus a [ref]: target definition) are valid Markdown and render identically, so rewriting common authority in that form left the guard with nothing to check, and expect(missing).toEqual([]) cannot distinguish an empty result from a clean one. MATERIAL: with the links in reference form, docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md could be deleted outright and the guard still passed. Verified by doing exactly that.
Same defect class this bead set out to close, relocated one layer down - from which identity the guard uses to which syntax it can see.
REPAIR, both halves required: read targets from both link forms; and fail when the guard finds NO targets at all, since common authority always points somewhere and an empty set means an unreadable syntax rather than a clean tree. Without the second half a third link form would reopen the hole silently.
ADVERSARIAL: green with every link rewritten reference-style and targets intact; red with reference-style links plus the policy unreachable (the exact state that passed before); red when links are stripped to a form the guard cannot parse.
PR #558 MERGED 2026-09-22 (merge commit c3171a28, reviewed head bc277005). Deliverable landed on main; bead closed. eshyra-5wbx (beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts, same defect class) is now unblocked.
